newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan December industrial output.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan December industrial output.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to Japan's industrial production for December, which showed a preliminary 0.3 percent rise from November on a seasonally adjusted basis. The Trade Ministry forecast that January output would rise 5.4 percent month on month while February output would fall 2.9 percent.

"It's exactly in line with my expectations. I think the key is really the forecasts...and they still point to quite strong first-quarter production. There is no sense that production is weaker than expected.
"I was a little bit surprised, I thought the scenario of the recovery of industrial production would be fairly firm based on exports of automobiles worldwide, especially to the United States."

"Basically, the 5.4 percent in January is in anticipation of a rush in demand (ahead of the consumption tax rise in April). I think the underlying trend is not terribly weak and it's also not terribly strong, it's kind of steady." But she added that if the anticipated extra demand in January failed to materialise "we may see a bit of a problem".

"It 0.3 and 0.8 was expected but this sort of difference is not really anything to worry about. If it was a change of one percent that would be different. Moreover, overall output for the October-December period was really quite high."

"Even though February is seen as a minus, the January to March period will probably still record a positive number. The problem is more what happens after fiscal '96/97. After the sales tax rises in April, the April-June quarter will definitely be negative. The question is whether lost ground can be made up in the July to September quarter."
